coverage_summary: Core OmicsLM projection, placeholder replacement, tokenizer, and alignment claims are largely supported. Blocking problems remain in the bulk composite-vector route, documented perturbation branches, protein-task evidence, TPM bypass semantics, and omitted fine-tuning loss-mask behavior.

findings.detail: The bulk composite-vector step uses project to create omics_vector from scaled expression, although the paper defines the vector as an ordered concatenation of four feature groups. No learned projection is documented at this point; the learned projection is a later operation.

evidence.quote: For each sample, the default input vector concatenates four feature groups: a one-dimensional input-scale indicator, the normalized expression vector, a 512-dimensional Funomics T0 embedding [Powalski et al., 2026], and a 768-dimensional embedding from Geneformer-V2104M [Chen et al., 2026], yielding a 20,541-dimensional omics vector.

findings.required_change: Replace this project call with the documented feature-stack construction, using concatenation for the four groups; retain the actual learned project call only in the subsequent omics-to-LLM step.

findings.detail: The bulk route omits the input-scale indicator, Funomics embedding, and Geneformer embedding from the documented default vector. The graph contains only aligned/scaled expression before omics_vector.

evidence.quote: For each sample, the default input vector concatenates four feature groups: a one-dimensional input-scale indicator, the normalized expression vector, a 512-dimensional Funomics T0 embedding [Powalski et al., 2026], and a 768-dimensional embedding from Geneformer-V2104M [Chen et al., 2026], yielding a 20,541-dimensional omics vector.
The input-scale indicator and learned embedding features are centered and scaled per dimension.

findings.required_change: Add the documented auxiliary feature inputs and their normalization branches, or preserve an opaque boundary that explicitly represents the complete composite vector rather than implying expression alone produces it.

findings.detail: The bulk TPM bypass connects bulk_tpm_aligned directly to omics_vector, thereby bypassing the entire composite-vector construction. Precomputed TPM only supports bypassing raw-count library-size normalization and log transformation; feature scaling and assembly remain documented.

evidence.quote: for bulk expression datasets, we used precomputed transcripts per million (TPM) values.
The feature groups are normalized before training to make their scales comparable.

findings.required_change: Move the bypass target to the post-TPM expression-preprocessing boundary and retain the documented feature normalization and concatenation before omics_vector.

findings.detail: The trajectory claims paired control/perturbed training tasks but supplies only control expression profiles. The paper documents a knockout-identification task with both control and perturbed profiles and a separate target-specific post-knockout task.

evidence.quote: Perturbation & Essentiality ... identifying knocked-out genes from paired control/perturbed expression profiles, and forecasting top expressed genes post-perturbation.
Given the control <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> and the perturbed <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> , determine the gene whose knockout caused this change.
Control expression profile: <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> <omics> List the 60 most highly expressed genes after knocking out METTL14.

findings.required_change: Add the perturbed-profile branch for knockout identification and preserve the perturbation-target context for post-knockout prediction; separate these documented task variants if their inputs differ.

findings.detail: The biological-knowledge trajectory's evidence supports pathway, network, and gene-set tasks but does not support the claimed protein-question branch or protein lexical mapping.

evidence.quote: pathway graphs, protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, and gene set collections do not provide transcriptomic profiles; they are used solely to construct natural-language graph-reasoning tasks over biological interaction networks and gene program annotations.
These were used to construct natural-language tasks requiring the model to answer questions about protein properties given a gene name.

Tasks linking expression profiles of cancer cell lines to copy-number alterations, mutated cancer genes, oncogenes, tumor suppressors, disease, lineage, and anatomical site, together with protein questions covering subcellular locations, protein functions, and enzymatic properties.

findings.required_change: Add the protein-resource evidence and preserve the protein-task source/context explicitly, or restrict this trajectory to the network, pathway, and gene-set tasks supported by its current evidence.

findings.detail: The GTEx bypass connects a TPM profile directly to omics_vector, omitting the documented composite feature interface and feature normalization. TPM status supports bypassing raw-count library-size/log preprocessing only.

evidence.quote: We use the v10 release, comprising 19,616 TPMnormalized samples spanning the full range of profiled tissues, which we use for tissue-of-origin prediction.

findings.detail: The fine-tuning trajectory marks decoder-side masking as unspecified, but the paper explicitly documents the supervised causal-language-model objective: assistant response tokens receive loss while user, system, and multimodal placeholder tokens are masked.
